notes: EnclosureSurface for Sphere in vendor/truck/truck-evidence/src/sphere.rs (scaffolding replaced; lib.rs and all sibling carriers untouched). enclose evaluates x/y/z from the certified crate pair crate::elementary::{cos,sin} on the whole cell (never endpoint-only) with inari interval products, so boxes straddling an interior extremum at k*pi/2 contain it. enclose_der(m, n) evaluates the same cyclic derivative table as truck-geometry's der_mn (u- and v-derivatives cycle every four orders), which is a closed form for every (m, n), so no order needs the whole-space fallback; each component is r times a product of one u-trig and one v-trig factor enclosed over (uu, vv). normal_cone uses the named const CONVEX_HALF_ANGLE = pi/2: below it the corner-average-axis cone is emitted (geodesically convex on the sphere), at or above it the everything-cone {axis: (0,0,1), half_angle: pi} (sound, not tight), with a near-zero corner-sum fallback (CORNER_SUM_MIN = 1e-14, an H-3-marked dimensionless threshold) for cancelling corner sets such as a u-range spanning both poles. The normal is radius-independent, so degenerate radii cannot break the method. immersion_lower_bound returns r^2 * sin(uu).inf().max(0.0), clamped at 0, which is exactly 0.0 at a pole box (the parameterization is singular there). Totality (H-1) holds for r <= 0 and non-finite r: interval arithmetic flows through without panicking. All six mandated tests added (sphere_encloses_sampled_points over five boxes incl. a full-azimuth band and a pole-containing box, sphere_trig_extrema_inside_interval asserting the z-enclosure contains cos(pi/2)=0 and the x-enclosure reaches the interior sin maximum, sphere_enclosure_converges_under_bisection at depth 20 on a pole-free box, sphere_normal_cone_over_patch for a small and a wide patch, sphere_immersion_lower_bound_and_poles, sphere_der_enclosures_match_partials for (1,0)/(0,1)/(2,0)). Every comparison epsilon carries a same-line // H-3 comment.
